landmark_cases.title: Friends of the Earth, Inc. v. Laidlaw Environmental Services (TOC), Inc.
landmark_cases.reason: Seminal Article III standing and mootness case explaining that civil penalties payable to the government can redress injury by deterring future violations, and setting the voluntary-cessation framework central to the remand on MFLSA penalties.

landmark_cases.title: Milner v. Farmers Ins. Exch.
landmark_cases.reason: Minnesota Supreme Court decision defining MFLSA remedies: private parties may seek the Commissioner’s remedies, but civil penalties are payable to the state; also addresses injunctive relief—foundational to the opinion’s MFLSA remedies analysis.

landmark_cases.title: Town of Chester, New York v. Laroe Estates, Inc.
landmark_cases.reason: Clarifies that a plaintiff must have standing for each claim and each form of relief sought—key to assessing standing for MFLSA civil penalties.

landmark_cases.title: City of Mesquite v. Aladdin’s Castle, Inc.
landmark_cases.reason: Canonical statement of the voluntary-cessation doctrine—that stopping challenged conduct does not automatically moot a case—relevant to whether Consilio’s policy moots the MFLSA penalties claim.

landmark_cases.title: United States v. Concentrated Phosphate Export Ass'n
landmark_cases.reason: Establishes the 'absolutely clear' standard for determining mootness after voluntary cessation—applied in evaluating whether the alleged violations could reasonably recur.
